source.title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)

accepted.question_text: In the category of real Banach spaces, is the Kalton-Peck space Z2 even, meaning that Z2 admits a bounded operator J with J^2 = -I_Z2, while no hyperplane of Z2 admits such a complex structure?

Does there exist a real Banach space X that is not isomorphic to its hyperplanes, such that X has complex structure and its hyperplanes also have complex structure? Here a real Banach space has complex structure when it admits a bounded operator J with J^2 = -I.

If X and Y are even real Banach spaces, must their direct sum X plus Y also be even without assuming that X and Y are totally incomparable? A real Banach space is even when it has complex structure but its hyperplanes do not.
accepted.context_brief: Direct sums of even Banach spaces

accepted.question_text: Is being an even real Banach space a 3-space property, meaning that whenever a closed subspace and the corresponding quotient space have the property, the whole Banach space must have the property?

Is having complex structure a 3-space property for real Banach spaces, meaning that whenever a closed subspace and the corresponding quotient space both admit a bounded operator whose square is minus the identity, the whole Banach space must also admit such an operator?

For an infinite-dimensional Banach space X with unit ball B and unit sphere S, determine the optimal Lipschitz retraction constant k0(X): the infimum of all k > 0 for which there exists a continuous retraction R from B onto S, equal to the identity on S, satisfying ||R(x)-R(y)|| <= k ||x-y|| for all x,y in B.

Does there exist an operator T from a Banach lattice X into a Banach space Y that is lattice-strictly singular but not disjointly strictly singular? Here T is lattice-strictly singular if it is not an isomorphism on any sublattice of X, and it is disjointly strictly singular if it is not an isomorphism on any subspace of X spanned by a disjoint sequence.
accepted.context_brief: Lattice-strictly singular versus disjointly strictly singular

accepted.question_text: Let E be a reflexive separable Banach lattice. Must E contain a disjoint sequence that spans a complemented subspace of E?

For every infinite-dimensional Banach space X, is the symmetric separation constant K_s(X) strictly greater than 1? Here K_s(X) is the supremum of all sigma > 0 for which there exists a sequence (x_n) in the unit ball B_X such that ||x_n + x_m|| >= sigma and ||x_n - x_m|| >= sigma whenever n != m.

For every Banach space X, does K(X**) = K(X), where X** is the bidual and K(X) is the supremum of all sigma > 0 for which the unit ball B_X contains a sequence (x_n) with ||x_n - x_m|| >= sigma whenever n != m?

For every Banach space X, does K_s(X**) = K_s(X), where X** is the bidual and K_s is the symmetric separation constant defined using sequences in the unit ball whose pairwise sums and differences both have norm at least a common separation value?

How many ultratypes of L_infty-spaces are there? Two Banach spaces X and Y have the same ultratype, or are ultra-isomorphic, when there is an ultrafilter U such that the ultrapowers X_U and Y_U are isomorphic.
Find additional Banach spaces X with the following property: whenever X is a subspace of a Banach space Z and the quotient Z/X is isomorphic to X, the subspace X is complemented in Z.

Characterize the compact spaces K for which the Banach space C(K) has the following property: whenever C(K) is a subspace of a Banach space Z and the quotient Z/C(K) is isomorphic to C(K), the subspace C(K) is complemented in Z.
For p > 2, does the classical sequence space ell_p contain continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces?
accepted.context_brief: Subspaces of ell_p for p greater than 2

accepted.question_text: In the standard Borel space SB of separable Banach spaces, besides the isomorphism class of ell_2, is there another example of a single isomorphism class that is itself a Borel subset of SB?
For p != 2, is the set of all separable Banach spaces that are isomorphic to ell_p a Borel subset of the standard Borel space SB of separable Banach spaces?

Is every Schauder basis of ell_1 randomly unconditionally divergent? A basis is randomly unconditionally divergent when there is a constant K such that each vector norm is bounded by K times the average, over independent signs, of the norm of the corresponding signed partial sums in the basis expansion.
Does every separable Aharoni space contain a linear copy of c0? A Banach space Y is an Aharoni space when every separable Banach space is Lipschitz-isomorphic to a subspace of Y.

Given 0 < delta <= 1, does there exist n0(delta) such that for every n >= n0(delta) and every family F of subsets of [n]^2 with |F| at least delta times 2^(n^2), there are A and B in F with A contained in B and B\A equal to X^2 for some subset X of [n]?

For bounded operators, were the following two equivalent assertions true: first, if T:L1(0,1)->L1(0,1) is bounded and T restricted to every subspace M isometric to ell_1 is an isomorphism, then T is an isomorphism; second, if T:ell_infty->ell_infty is bounded and has dense range, then T is surjective?

Question 11. Does L_p contain a continuum of non-isomorphic subspaces?
Conjecture 3. Let f:S_c0 -> R be uniformly continuous, where S_c0 = A union B, and let epsilon > 0. Then there exist infinitely many block subspaces Z of c0 such that S_Z is contained in A_epsilon.
